title: Lost but not erased: Finding traces of a forgotten language in neural speech models
abstract: arXiv:2608.25976v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: International adoptees retain phonological traces of a birth language they can no longer speak or comprehend, a persistence typically attributed to a biologically-timed critical period. We asked whether it could instead reflect the ordinary dynamics of learning, using automatic speech recognition models that simulate the international adoptee experience without maturational confounds. Models were trained on one language and then abruptly switched to a second. We found that traces of the first language persisted throughout second-language training, but mainly in the lowest, pre-phonemic layers. These traces were functional, as models with early exposure re-learned their lost first language 14% faster than naive models; this advantage held even against models adopted early from a related language and disappeared when the earliest layers were substituted from a non-adopted model. We argue that these critical-period effects reflect entrenchm

translated_title: 被遗忘却未抹去：在神经语音模型中寻找一门被遗忘语言的痕迹
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25976v1 公告类型：新 摘要：国际收养者保留了他们无法再说或理解的原生语言的语音痕迹，这种持久性通常归因于生物时间上的关键期。我们提出，这可能反映了学习的普通动态，通过使用自动语音识别模型来模拟国际收养者的经历，而无需考虑成熟混淆因素。模型先训练于一种语言，然后突然切换到第二种语言。我们发现，第一种语言的痕迹在整个第二语言训练过程中持续存在，但主要集中在最低的、前音素层。这些痕迹具有功能性，因为早期接触的模型重新学习其丢失的第一语言比新模型快14%；这一优势甚至在与从相关语言早期收养的模型比较时仍然存在，并在最早层被非收养模型替代时消失。我们认为，这些关键期效应反映了固化。
tldr: 本文通过语音识别模型模拟国际收养经历，发现被遗忘语言的痕迹主要保留在最低前音素层，且早期接触能加速重新学习，表明关键期效应源于学习动态中的固化而非生物时间限制。
en_tdlr: This paper uses speech recognition models to simulate international adoptee experiences, finding that traces of a forgotten language persist mainly in the lowest pre-phonemic layers, and early exposure accelerates relearning, suggesting critical-period effects arise from entrenchment in learning dynamics rather than biological timing.
